summary: Section 461 of the Companies Act, 2013 requires the Central Government to prepare a general annual report on how this law is working and administered. This report must then be presented to both Houses of Parliament. The entire process must be completed within one year after the end of the year covered by the report.
points: The Central Government must prepare a general annual report.
The report covers the working and administration of the Companies Act.
The completed report must be laid before each House of Parliament.
The submission to Parliament must happen within one year of the close of the year the report relates to.
example: Asha Trading Private Limited operates in Mumbai and often reviews government regulations. At the end of the financial year, the Central Government finalizes a comprehensive general annual report detailing the working and administration of the Companies Act, 2013. To fulfill its legal obligation under Section 461, the government ensures that this newly prepared report is formally presented and laid before both the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha within one year from the close of the year for which the report was prepared. This procedure keeps the Parliament informed about how the company law is being administered across the country.

terms.term: Laid before each House of Parliament
terms.meaning: Presented officially to both the upper and lower houses of the country's legislature for their review.
The process of managing and running the affairs related to the law.

watch: Do not confuse the one-year deadline for presenting the report to Parliament with other shorter deadlines found elsewhere in the Act.
